title: Seventy-Six All Out. Archer and Tongue Rip Through India for England's Biggest-Ever T20 Win.
excerpt: World champions bowled out in 11.4 overs — their lowest total in 18 years and heaviest defeat in T20I history — as England seize a 2-0 series lead with two to play
body:
India's tour of England hit its lowest point on Tuesday as the world champions were bowled out for 76 at Trent Bridge — their second-lowest T20I score in history and their heaviest defeat in the format. England's 125-run demolition hands the hosts a 2-0 series lead with two matches to play and raises urgent questions about India's ability to compete overseas against genuine pace.

## Archer and Tongue Set the Tone

Chasing a stiff target of 202, India's batting order collapsed under a relentless pace barrage from Jofra Archer and Josh Tongue. The pair shared seven wickets between them — Tongue finishing with 4-28 from four overs, Archer with 3-29 from three — as India lost five wickets inside the first six overs for the first time in their T20I history.

The trouble began early. Abhishek Sharma fell for 10, caught at deep point off Tongue, before 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi — who had smashed two audacious sixes in a five-ball 13 — gloved a well-directed Archer bouncer through to Jos Buttler. Ishan Kishan and Shreyas Iyer then departed in successive deliveries to catches from Jacob Bethell, and Axar Patel's brief counter-attack ended when Archer's extra bounce found the edge. India were 52-5 after five overs, and there was no way back.

Only 24 more runs were added as the remaining batters offered token resistance. The innings was over in 11.4 overs — the quickest India have ever been bowled out in T20Is, smashing the previous record of 17.2 overs set in 2015. Captain Shreyas Iyer called it \"atrocious.\"

## Salt Powers England's Total

England had set the platform with a commanding 201-7, anchored by Phil Salt's destructive 70 from 44 balls. Salt played out a maiden to Arshdeep Singh before accelerating with three sixes that took the game away from India's bowlers.

India's new-ball pair had their moments. Prince Yadav, in just his third T20I, impressed with 2-30, including a beautiful inswinging yorker to dismiss Buttler for 36. Harshit Rana struck twice in consecutive balls, removing Bethell and Tom Banton. But Sam Curran's unbeaten 41 from 24 balls propelled England past 200.

## A Worrying Pattern Emerges

The collapse exposed a recurring technical vulnerability that has plagued India overseas. Against hard-length bowling in the 6-10 metre band, India's batters have averaged just 14.29 in this series — a dramatic decline from the 47.70 they managed on home soil during the T20 World Cup. The contrast between their home and away performances against pace has become impossible to ignore.

This is now India's third consecutive completed T20I loss, a streak they haven't experienced since 2021. Having already fallen 2-0 in Ireland before arriving in England, captain Iyer acknowledged the scale of the problem: \"Losing by such a big margin isn't acceptable. We have to go back to the drawing board.\"

## What It Means for the Diaspora

For the thousands of Indian fans who packed Trent Bridge — and the millions watching across time zones from New York to San Francisco — the result stings. England are now on course to dislodge India as the world's No. 1 ranked T20I side, with Harry Brook's team having won 18 of their last 21 matches in the format.

The series moves to Bristol's County Ground on Thursday for the fourth T20I, with India needing to win both remaining matches to salvage a draw. Whether Iyer reshuffles the batting order — particularly the question of Sanju Samson's exclusion despite being the T20 World Cup's Player of the Tournament — will dominate the conversation among fans and pundits alike.

*Sources: Reuters, Cricbuzz, The Times*
